text: RELEASE OBSTACLE REMOVED, no scanner change, not a dependency. Your scanner correctly refuses 14 of Samuel's own PDFs (8 DAYHANA_INTERNAL_*, XENIOS_COMPLETE_CUSTOMER_CATALOG, 3 MITCH revenue-share versions, SETH advisor V3/V4) because their exporter attached C2PA Content Credentials. Rather than ask you to loosen the rule, I shipped scripts/resource-hub/strip-embedded-attachments.mjs at a39f0c95bc9f6dc1de39d4a91d15ae25298f1e5f (tree d87f26082c0374a39a1cfcf246ea8cfabd7a863d) on fable/recruiter-resource-hub-20260906. It deletes every object reachable from /Names /EmbeddedFiles and from /AF on the catalog and each page, and never writes over its input. Unlinking the name tree alone is NOT enough: an unreferenced attachment is still serialized and still reads as /EmbeddedFile. Measured against YOUR scanner at 33436c5: refuse 14/14 before, accept 14/14 after; zero /EmbeddedFile, /EF or /Filespec left; 94 of 94 pages preserved with byte-identical decoded page content streams and identical page sizes, so nothing a reader sees changed. Evidence: republishable/strip-journal.jsonl and republishable/republish-scanner-verdicts.json in the QA evidence dir; docs/resource-hub/SCANNER_SUPERSESSION_AND_PUBLISHABILITY.md has the full record. It is a standalone operator script under scripts/ — it touches no server, shared or client path, and I did NOT change vitest.config.ts during your freeze, so picking it up cannot force re-qualification. /OpenAction is deliberately untouched: removing an action the scanner cannot resolve is your policy call, not a cleanup, so s41587-026-03019-1.pdf (a third-party Nature paper) stays refused. Take it or leave it out of the RC; nothing depends on me.
